t: A policy issued in June 2024 is sought to be repudiated in 2026 on the ground of a non-fraudulent misstatement of a material fact. Under Section 45, which of the following is correct?
o: The insurer may repudiate and forfeit all premiums paid
The insurer may repudiate within 3 years but must refund the premiums collected up to the date of repudiation to the policyholder or nominee
The insurer must pay the full sum assured and then recover the extra premium
The insurer cannot repudiate at all because the misstatement was not fraudulent
e: For misstatement or suppression that is not fraud, Section 45 allows repudiation within 3 years with refund of premiums paid; forfeiture applies only on proven fraud.

t: Ramesh has lent ₹20 lakh to Suresh. On whose life, and up to what amount, does Ramesh have insurable interest as a creditor?
o: On his own life only, for ₹20 lakh
On Suresh's life, for any amount Ramesh chooses
On Suresh's life, limited to the outstanding debt (₹20 lakh) plus interest and the cost of insurance
On Suresh's life for exactly twice the loan amount
e: A creditor's insurable interest in the debtor's life is limited to the extent of the debt (with interest and premium cost); any higher cover is speculative.

t: In life insurance, insurable interest must exist at which point in time?
o: At any time during the policy term
At the time the contract is effected (proposal/inception)
At the time of claim only
Both at inception and at the time of claim
e: Unlike marine and general insurance, life insurance requires insurable interest only at inception, which is why assignment to a person without insurable interest is permitted.

t: The mortality table currently used as the basis for pricing individual life insurance in India is:
e: IRDAI and the Institute of Actuaries of India adopted IALM 2012-14 as the current standard mortality table for assured lives, replacing IALM 2006-08.

t: Which document is the primary source of information for the life underwriter?
o: The proposal form with its declarations
e: The proposal form, signed by the proposer, is the basis of the contract and the primary source; other reports supplement and verify it.

t: The agent is often described as the 'primary' or 'field' underwriter because:
o: The agent meets the proposer personally and is the first to screen and report on the risk
The agent fixes the extra premium for substandard lives
The agent conducts the medical examination
The agent has authority to accept or decline proposals
e: Through personal contact the agent is the first to assess the proposer and submits a confidential report; the agent has no authority to accept risks or fix premiums.

t: A moral hazard report is typically called for by a life insurer in which situation?
o: Proposals for large sums assured or on the life of another person
Only when the proposer is above 60 years
Only when the proposer is a woman
e: The moral hazard report, prepared by an official of the insurer, verifies the proposer's standing, insurance needs and intentions in high-value or third-party cases.

t: As per the IRDAI master circular on protection of policyholders' interests (2024), a life insurer must decide on a proposal within how many days of receiving the complete proposal?
e: The 2024 norms tightened the earlier 15-day requirement to 7 days from receipt of the proposal with all requirements.

t: An automated underwriting engine (straight-through processing) in a life insurer:
o: Applies pre-set rules to issue clean cases automatically and refers exceptions to a human underwriter
Replaces the need for any medical examination at all ages
Is used only for reinsurance treaties
e: Rule engines speed issuance of standard risks; cases with adverse disclosures or high sums assured are routed to underwriters.

t: A flat extra premium of ₹3 per thousand sum assured is imposed for occupational hazard on a policy of ₹8 lakh. The annual extra premium is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Flat extra = ₹3 × (8,00,000 / 1,000) = ₹3 × 800 = ₹2,400 per annum.

t: The role of the medical referee (Chief Medical Officer) in a life insurer's underwriting structure is to:
o: Advise underwriters on the significance and rating of medical impairments
e: The medical referee interprets reports and medical evidence; the lay underwriter combines this advice with non-medical factors to reach a decision.

t: Which of the following forms part of the life insurance contract?
o: The proposal form and the declarations made therein
e: The proposal and declarations are the basis of the contract and are referred to in the policy document; the other items are not contractual.

t: Partnership insurance is taken by partners on each other's lives primarily to:
o: Increase the firm's working capital borrowing limit
Provide funds to buy out the deceased partner's share so that the firm can continue
Pay the deceased partner's personal income tax
e: On a partner's death, the surviving partners need liquidity to pay the deceased's estate; cover is based on the partner's share of capital and goodwill.

t: In an employer-employee insurance scheme, the employer has insurable interest in the employee's life because:
o: The premium is exempt from GST
The employer stands to suffer financial loss from the death of the employee
The employee's family is related to the employer
Employers must insure all employees under the Insurance Act
e: Insurable interest arises from the economic value of the employee's services to the employer.

t: A housewife with no independent income proposes a ₹1 crore policy; her husband's own life cover is ₹20 lakh. The underwriter is most likely to:
o: Accept the full ₹1 crore as there is no mortality risk
Restrict her cover with reference to the husband's existing insurance and income, since her cover should not exceed his
Accept only if the policy is a term plan
Decline because women without income cannot be insured
e: For non-earning spouses, cover is usually linked to and limited by the earning spouse's insurance and income to avoid moral hazard.

t: A 30-year-old with mild intermittent asthma, using an inhaler occasionally with no hospitalisation, is usually underwritten as:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Mild, well-controlled asthma carries negligible extra mortality; severe asthma with hospital admissions, steroid dependence or ICU care is rated significantly.

t: The sum assured under a loan-protection (credit life) policy taken by a borrower is generally:
o: Unlimited, as the bank has unlimited insurable interest
At least five times the loan amount
Limited to the outstanding loan amount, often on a decreasing basis
Fixed at ₹1 crore for all borrowers
e: A creditor's insurable interest extends only to the debt; mortgage redemption plans reduce cover in line with the loan schedule.

t: For a policy issued after 1 April 2012, the deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act for life insurance premium is available only to the extent the premium does not exceed:
e: Premium above 10% of the actual capital sum assured is not deductible (20% for policies issued before 1 April 2012; 15% for persons with specified disability/disease).

t: The residential risk of an NRI proposer living in a foreign country is assessed mainly on:
o: The exchange rate of that country's currency
Political stability, climate, sanitation, availability of medical care and prevalence of disease in that country
The distance of the country from India
The number of Indian restaurants in that country
e: Country classification for underwriting reflects mortality-related conditions; war zones and areas with poor health infrastructure are rated or declined.

t: Prolonged occupational exposure to asbestos is associated with which disease?
e: Asbestos fibres cause asbestosis (lung fibrosis) and mesothelioma; silica causes silicosis and coal dust causes pneumoconiosis.

t: Occupational exposure to benzene is linked to an increased risk of:
e: Benzene is a known cause of leukaemia and other blood disorders, relevant for chemical and petroleum industry workers.

t: Under a 40% quota share treaty, on a policy with sum assured ₹50 lakh the reinsurer's share is:
e: Quota share cedes a fixed percentage of every risk: 40% × ₹50 lakh = ₹20 lakh.

t: Under 'risk premium' (yearly renewable term) reinsurance, the reinsurer:
o: Covers the sum at risk for a premium recalculated each year, without sharing the policy's reserves
Pays a share of bonuses to the policyholder
Shares the original premium and reserves in the same proportion as the sum assured
e: YRT reinsurance insures the net amount at risk; original-terms (coinsurance) reinsurance shares premiums, reserves and commissions.

t: Catastrophe excess-of-loss reinsurance for a life insurer is designed to protect against:
o: Multiple deaths arising from a single event, such as an accident involving many members of a group scheme
e: Cat XL responds when one event causes claims above a stated amount; it is non-proportional and common for group business.

t: In a life reinsurance treaty, the 'jumbo limit' refers to:
o: The number of lives a group scheme must have
The highest premium rate the reinsurer may charge
The maximum total insurance in force and applied for on one life, across all insurers, beyond which automatic cover is not available
The minimum size of the treaty
e: If total cover on a life exceeds the jumbo limit, the case must be submitted facultatively even if within the cedant's treaty lines.

t: Haemophilia A is characterised by:
o: An excess of red blood cells causing thrombosis
An inherited deficiency of clotting factor VIII, transmitted on the X chromosome and affecting mainly males
Abnormal haemoglobin that sickles under low oxygen
e: Haemophilia is a sex-linked bleeding disorder; underwriting depends on severity (factor level), bleeding history and access to factor replacement.

t: Which type of blood cancer is most commonly seen in elderly persons and often runs an indolent course?
e: CLL typically affects older adults and may need no treatment for years; acute leukaemias are aggressive and require postponement or declinature.

t: Investigation of an early death claim (within 3 years of issue) to check for non-disclosure at proposal stage is sometimes referred to as:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Early claims are investigated for material non-disclosure since Section 45 permits repudiation within 3 years; this is effectively underwriting at claim stage.

t: 'Petit mal' (absence) seizures:
o: Are a complication of stroke in the elderly
Involve violent convulsions with loss of bladder control
Occur mostly in children as brief lapses of awareness and often resolve with age
e: Absence seizures are a childhood epilepsy with a good prognosis; grand mal (tonic-clonic) seizures involve convulsions.

t: A proposer suffered a stroke (CVA) four months ago and has recovered with mild residual weakness. The appropriate underwriting decision is:
o: Accept with an age set-back of 3 years
Postpone, usually for 6-12 months from the event, and then rate according to residual deficit and risk factors
e: Early recurrence risk after stroke is high, so a postponement period is followed by a rating based on cause, deficit, blood pressure and diabetes.

t: The HbA1c test reflects average blood glucose control over the preceding:
e: Glycated haemoglobin reflects glucose exposure over the lifespan of red cells (about 120 days), making it the key control marker for underwriters.

t: Which of the following are microvascular complications of diabetes?
e: Microvascular complications affect the small vessels of the eye, kidney and nerves; macrovascular complications are coronary, cerebral and peripheral arterial disease.

t: The earliest laboratory sign of diabetic kidney disease (nephropathy) is:
e: Small amounts of albumin in urine appear before creatinine rises; its presence in a diabetic proposer worsens the rating considerably.

t: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act 1938 requires that:
o: Premium is received in advance before the risk is assumed
Every policy carries a free-look clause
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). No risk may be assumed unless the premium has been received in advance or is guaranteed in the manner prescribed.

t: A 35-year-old woman on levothyroxine 50 mcg daily for hypothyroidism has had normal TSH for the past year. The usual underwriting decision is:
e: Treated hypothyroidism with normal thyroid function carries no significant extra mortality.

t: Untreated or poorly controlled hyperthyroidism concerns the underwriter mainly because of:
o: Cardiac complications such as atrial fibrillation and heart failure
e: Thyrotoxicosis strains the heart; once controlled (euthyroid) for a reasonable period, standard or near-standard terms are usual.

t: The normal range of serum creatinine in adults is approximately:
e: Serum creatinine rises as kidney function falls; values above the normal range call for eGFR estimation and nephrology assessment.

t: Chronic kidney disease stage 5 (end-stage renal disease) is defined by an estimated GFR below:
e: Stage 3 is eGFR 30-59, stage 4 is 15-29 and stage 5 (<15) usually requires dialysis or transplant and is declined.

t: A proposer completed a full course of anti-tuberculosis treatment for pulmonary TB 18 months ago and has been declared cured with no symptoms. The usual decision is:
o: Standard, or a small temporary extra depending on the insurer's guidelines
e: Treated and cured TB has little long-term mortality impact; active or recently treated TB is postponed until treatment is complete and cure confirmed.

t: A proposer who has smoked 30 cigarettes a day for 20 years has a smoking history of:
e: Pack-years = (cigarettes per day / 20) × years smoked = (30/20) × 20 = 30 pack-years.

t: A hepatitis B carrier with persistently normal liver function tests and normal ultrasound is usually:
o: Accepted with a mild to moderate extra, reflecting the long-term risk of cirrhosis and liver cancer
e: Inactive carriers have modest extra risk; chronic active hepatitis with raised enzymes or fibrosis is rated heavily and cirrhosis is declined.

t: Which liver enzyme is most specifically raised by excessive alcohol consumption?
e: GGT, especially with raised MCV and AST:ALT ratio above 2, points to alcohol excess; this is a key check against habit declarations.

t: A positive treadmill (exercise ECG) test is indicated by:
o: ST-segment depression of 1 mm or more during exercise, suggesting myocardial ischaemia
A rise in heart rate with exercise
e: Exercise-induced ST depression suggests coronary artery disease; such cases need further evaluation such as angiography before a decision.

t: A proposer suffered a myocardial infarction four months ago. The standard underwriting approach is:
o: Accept with a 20% lien for one year
Postpone, usually for 6-12 months, then rate according to ejection fraction, residual ischaemia and risk factors
Accept at standard rates if he feels well
e: Early post-infarction mortality is high; after the postponement period, the extent of damage and control of risk factors determine the rating.

t: Nomination and assignment of a life insurance policy are governed respectively by which sections of the Insurance Act 1938?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 39 deals with nomination; Section 38 with assignment and transfer.

t: Coronary angioplasty with stent placement for single-vessel disease, done 2 years ago with no symptoms since, is usually:
o: Rated with a moderate to substantial extra depending on cardiac function and risk factors
Standard, as the blockage has been removed
e: Revascularisation treats the lesion but not the underlying atherosclerosis; ongoing risk justifies a rating.

t: Unstable angina differs from stable angina in that it:
o: Occurs only during exercise and is relieved by rest
Occurs at rest or with increasing frequency and severity, signalling an impending infarction, and warrants postponement
e: Unstable angina is an acute coronary syndrome; stable effort angina is rated according to severity and investigation results.

topic: Special Senses: Disorders of the Eyes, Ears and Nose
t: A proposer with a treated retinal detachment and restored vision is usually:
o: Accepted at standard rates for life cover
e: Retinal detachment, often linked to high myopia or trauma, does not affect life expectancy once treated.

topic: Special Senses: Disorders of the Eyes, Ears and Nose
t: A totally blind proposer applies for life cover and an accidental death benefit rider. The usual approach is:
o: Both declined as blindness is uninsurable
Life cover declined but ADB accepted
Life cover at or near standard rates, but the ADB rider restricted or declined because of accident exposure
e: Blindness has little effect on mortality but substantially raises accident risk, which affects accident and disability riders.

topic: Special Senses: Disorders of the Eyes, Ears and Nose
t: Retinitis pigmentosa is:
o: A hereditary degeneration of the retina causing night blindness and progressive visual field loss
A curable bacterial infection of the retina
e: Life cover is usually standard; the progressive visual loss affects accident and disability riders.
